text: A few miles from Boston. <break time="0.8s" /> In Massachusetts. <break time="0.8s" /> A narrow inlet winds far into the country. <break time="0.8s" /> And ends in a thickly wooded swamp. <break time="0.8s" /> According to an old story. <break time="0.8s" /> Kidd the pirate buried a great treasure. <break time="0.8s" /> Under one of the giant oaks. <break time="0.8s" /> That stand beside this inlet. <break time="0.8s" /> Kidd never returned for it. <break time="0.8s" /> Because soon afterward he was arrested in Boston. <break time="0.8s" /> Sent to England. <break time="0.8s" /> And executed as a pirate. <break time="0.8s" /> People also say. <break time="0.8s" /> That the devil himself watched over the hiding of the gold. <break time="0.8s" /> And has guarded it closely ever since. <break time="0.8s" /> About the year 1727. <break time="0.8s" /> There lived near this place. <break time="0.8s" /> A mean, greedy man named Tom Walker. <break time="0.8s" /> Who had a wife as miserly as himself. <break time="0.8s" /> So miserly were the two. <break time="0.8s" /> That they even tried to cheat each other. <break time="0.8s" /> And whatever the wife could get her hands on she hid away. <break time="0.8s" /> They quarreled so loudly and so often. <break time="0.8s" /> That a lonely traveler passing their house. <break time="0.8s" /> Would stop to listen. <break time="0.8s" /> And then hurry on his way. <break time="0.8s" /> Their house stood alone in a bare field. <break time="0.8s" /> And like its owners. <break time="0.8s" /> It had a hungry, half starved look about it. <break time="0.8s" /> A miserable horse. <break time="0.8s" /> Its ribs showing like the bars of a grill. <break time="0.8s" /> Wandered about the field. <break time="0.8s" /> In search of something to eat.
